questions.statement: Which auxiliary verb is used to form the Present Perfect?
questions.context: Identifying the structure of the Present Perfect.

options.feedback: Incorrect. This is for Present Simple.
Incorrect. This is for Past Continuous or Past of be.
Correct! Present Perfect uses have or has as an auxiliary.

questions.explanation:
The student identifies the basic auxiliary verb for the Present Perfect tense.

questions.statement: What instrument(s) has Valentina played in her life?
questions.context:
A conversation between two students about hobbies.
Andrés: "Have you ever played a musical instrument?"
Valentina: "Yes, I have played the guitar since I was 10. I have also tried the piano, but I didn't like it."

options.feedback: Incorrect. She also tried the piano.

options.text: Both the guitar and the piano.

questions.explanation:
The student applies reading strategies to identify experiences expressed in the Present Perfect.

questions.statement: Which sentence describes an experience at an UNSPECIFIED time?
questions.context: Distinguishing between Present Perfect and Past Simple.

options.text: I went to Cali last year.
I saw my friend two hours ago.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Time is specified (two hours ago).

options.text: I have visited Cali several times.
options.feedback: Correct! The specific times are not mentioned, only the fact of the experience.

questions.explanation:
The student analyzes the difference between specific past time (Simple) and general life experience (Perfect).

questions.statement: What can we analyze about Mateo's life from this list?
questions.context:
Analyzing a list of achievements.
"Mateo's achievements: 1. He has won a soccer tournament. 2. He has learned to speak French. 3. He has traveled to three different continents."

options.text: He is a very lazy person.
He is an active person with diverse interests and international experiences.
options.feedback: Correct! Sport, language, and travel are diverse and active.
Incorrect. He also learned a language and traveled.

options.text: He has never left his city.
options.feedback: Incorrect. He has traveled to three continents.

questions.explanation:
The student analyzes a set of perfect tense statements to infer general characteristics about a person's life.

questions.statement: Does the candidate have experience working with others?
questions.context:
Evaluating an interview response.
Interviewer: "Have you ever worked in a team?"
Candidate: "Yes, I have worked in many school teams. We have completed many projects together. I have always been the leader."

options.text: Yes, they have experience in collaborative tasks and leadership roles.
options.feedback: Correct! "Worked in many school teams" and "been the leader" support this.

options.text: No, they only worked by themselves.
Yes, but they only worked on one project.
No, because school teams are not real experience.
options.feedback: Incorrect. In a school context, it is valid experience.

questions.explanation: The student evaluates the evidence provided in a perfect tense response to confirm a candidate's background and skills.
